en.headline: Wong Tai Sin lantern display runs through Sunday
en.dek: Sik Sik Yuen is keeping the temple open later until 4 October for a free Mid-Autumn lantern display marking its 105th anniversary.
body: Sik Sik Yuen's Mid-Autumn lantern display at Wong Tai Sin Temple runs through Sunday, the last night of an 18-day programme that opened on 17 September. The organisers said the event also marks the 77th anniversary of National Day and the temple charity's 105th anniversary.

Admission is free. The temple is staying open until 10pm on Saturday and Sunday, and until 9pm on weekdays, for the display in the temple and the temple square. Lanterns made with traditional framing include familiar Mid-Autumn shapes and a set made for the temple, among them a lantern of a Hong Kong astronaut at launch, the organisers said.

Sik Sik Yuen said the programme also includes lantern riddles and a stargazing session. A lantern-making workshop is listed for Sunday evening from 6pm to 9:30pm at Fung Ming Hall. The display ends on 4 October.

zh.headline: 黃大仙祠中秋綵燈展延至周日
zh.dek: 嗇色園黃大仙祠中秋綵燈晚會免費入場，周六及周日延長開放至晚上十時，展期至十月四日。
body: 嗇色園黃大仙祠的中秋綵燈展將於周日最後一晚結束。主辦方表示，活動由九月十七日展開，為期十八天，並配合國慶七十七周年及嗇色園一百零五周年。
活動免費入場。祠內及廟宇廣場展出傳統紮作花燈，包括經典中秋造型、黃大仙祠專屬花燈，以及一組香港太空人升空造型花燈。周六、日及公眾假期祠廟延長開放至晚上十時，平日則至晚上九時。
嗇色園表示，場內另有猜燈謎及觀星體驗。周日晚上六時至九時三十分，鳳鳴樓禮堂設有花燈工作坊。展覽於十月四日結束。
